newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan raises fuel oil bunker price on Gulf fears.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan raises fuel oil bunker price on Gulf fears.

text.p: Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has raised its spot and term prices of bunker fuel effective September 6, a company statement said on Monday.

Posted prices for 180-, 280- and 380-centistoke bunker fuel delivered at the ports of Keelung, Hualien, Taichung and Suao were increased by a hefty $15, at $135 per tonne. Term prices were also raised by $15, at $123.
Spot and term bunker C grade was also up by $15, at $138 and $138 respectively.
CPC official told Reuters that the jump in prices was a result of a recent hike in oil prices following the US-Iraq conflict.
"We were concerned with security of oil and the political stability of the Middle Wast after the conflict started," the official said.
"We may lower the prices later," he added.
CPC is state owned and the country's sole supplier of bunker fuels.
